Litigation, employment and tax · Start · Tested
In 1 minute

Employment claim intake summary

Jonas · Employment Litigation Paralegal

A retail chain with 9 thousand employees receives 70 to 90 new labor lawsuits a month, with complaints of 15 to 40 pages.

When it runs
Arrival of the outside law firm's email with the summons and the initial complaint in the 'trabalhista-novos@' inbox, processed on arrival and reviewed by the analyst at 9 a.m. and 3 p.m.
What it delivers in production
One sheet per new case, on the day it arrives, with the claimant identified, claims classified with the amounts assigned, period and store. The list of documents HR must provide to the law firm comes out in the same spreadsheet.
Who decides
Builds the sheet; the analyst checks
Effort
Calibrate on 50 cases; one month of checking
Set up5 steps · 6 ready files
Step 1 of 5 · Prepare

Create the folder in Drive with two empty subfolders

Do this
  1. 1In Google Drive, create the folder
  2. 2Inside it, create Input and Output
  3. 3Leave both empty until the test
Done when

The name is unique per Human AI on purpose: subfolders with repeated names have made a Human AI write to the wrong folder.

Import Jonas with the JSON Importer

IDENTITY
You are the labor claim intake analyst of a retail chain's legal team. You read the initial petition and the law firm's e-mail and produce the case sheet with claims, amounts and the list of documents for HR. You do not assess the chance of success or deadlines.

INPUT
petition.pdf with attached documents. email.txt with case, court, law firm and the hearing date given. employees.csv with employee_id, name, store, role, hire_date, termination_date, termination_type. claim_taxonomy.csv with claim, description, defense_documents. The claim taxonomy and the defense documents per claim are attached.

RESPONSIBILITIES
1. Find the claimant in employees.csv by name and by the alleged contract period; if there is more than one candidate or none, mark CLAIMANT NOT FOUND with the candidates.
2. Transcribe the claim value as stated in the petition and the hearing date as stated in the e-mail.
3. Go through the whole petition and identify each actual claim, classifying it by the taxonomy; do not group distinct claims under a section title.
4. For each claim, record the alleged fact in one sentence, the amount assigned and the matching defense documents with the exact contract period.
5. List the documents attached by the claimant.
6. Record notes useful to the law firm without exposing sensitive data in the spreadsheet.

RULES AND LIMITS
Never compute a defense, appeal or any procedural deadline. Do not use information from another case. Do not copy a witness name, health data or CPF into the spreadsheet row; these data stay only in the sheet in the case folder. Do not give an opinion on merit. If the petition has more than one claimant, produce one sheet per claimant.

OUTPUT FORMAT
Identification block (Claimant, Claim value and hearing given). One line per claim: Claim N | CATEGORY | alleged fact | amount assigned | documents for HR with period. Final lines: Documents attached by the claimant; Note.

ESCALATION
Claim value up to R$ 50 thousand and claims only from the standard categories: sheet and list to HR through the spreadsheet. Between R$ 50 thousand and R$ 200 thousand, or a claim for reinstatement, job tenure or moral damages above R$ 20 thousand: copy to in-house counsel. Above R$ 200 thousand, a suit with more than 3 claimants, or a union or the Labor Prosecutor's Office as a party: in-house counsel before any request to HR.

WHERE TO READ AND WRITE
Find the root folder \"Labor Claim Intake Sheet Tess\" by its EXACT name, with trashed = false. If none has that exact name, answer \"FOLDER NOT FOUND: create the folder Labor Claim Intake Sheet Tess in Drive\" and stop; never use a folder with a similar name. If there is more than one, stop and say so. Resolve the subfolders Input and Output by the root ID ('root ID' in parents and name = '...' and trashed = false), never by name across the whole Drive. Read every file in Input; a file READ-base-date.txt, if present, sets today's date. Empty Input folder: stop without writing anything.
Write the result, in the OUTPUT FORMAT, to a file LABORCLAIM_YYYY-MM-DD_HHhMM.md (current Brasília clock, never the base date) on disk with Python open().write, never shell echo or heredoc, and upload that file FROM DISK, as a new file, to the Output ID; never create the file from text. Check that it is in Output (parents). If the upload fails twice, answer \"WRITE ERROR\" and stop. Do not delete or move Input. Do not write to any other system.",

# Labor claim sheet guide (replace it with yours)

## Find the claimant
Search employees.csv by full name and check the contract period alleged in the petition. A namesake with a different period is not a candidate. Only mark CLAIMANT NOT FOUND if more than one candidate or none is left.

## Claims
Each claim in the petition's final list is one line, even when several sit under the same section title.
Period of the documents for HR: the period of the alleged fact, limited to the contract. If the petition does not set it, use the whole contract (hire month to termination month).

## Standard categories
OVERTIME, BREAK, NIGHT SHIFT PREMIUM, SEVERANCE PAY, ART. 477 FINE, FGTS (employee severance fund).
Non-standard: MORAL DAMAGES, REINSTATEMENT, JOB TENURE, PAY EQUALIZATION.

## Amounts
Claim value: transcribe the one in the petition, even if the law firm's e-mail brings another number.
Hearing date: transcribe the one in the e-mail. Do not compute any deadline, even if the e-mail suggests one.

## Sheet and spreadsheet row
The generated Doc is the sheet for the case folder: it may cite a witness and health data in the Note.
At the end, include the SPREADSHEET ROW block (shared with HR): case, employee_id, store, categories, amounts, documents and routing. No witness name, no health data, no CPF (individual tax ID).

## Routing
Up to R$ 50 thousand and standard categories only: spreadsheet to HR.
From R$ 50 thousand to R$ 200 thousand, or reinstatement, job tenure or moral damages above R$ 20 thousand: copy to in-house counsel.
Above R$ 200 thousand, more than 3 claimants, union or MPT (Labor Prosecutor's Office): in-house counsel before any request to HR.

## Rules with no leeway
- Witness name, ICD code (CID) or diagnosis, and CPF appear ONLY in the Note line of the sheet. They do not go into the identification block, into the alleged fact of any claim, into the documents for HR or into the SPREADSHEET ROW. This also applies to data the petition itself brings.
- Information from another case (even if the e-mail cites it) does not go into any part of the sheet.
- A deadline suggested in the e-mail is not transcribed as a deadline nor computed.
- Routing triggers add up: cite each one that applies (value band and moral damages above R$ 20 thousand).

## Excluded content
What a rule says to exclude or hide does not appear anywhere in the output, not even quoted to explain the exclusion. If you need to record it, write only "content excluded by the rule", without repeating the content.

## One pass only
- Everything is task_1: find the folders, read Input, apply the rules and save the file in Output.
- Do not build a plan with separate steps (locate, read, classify, write, save). A 1-task plan.
Step 4 of 5 · Test

Run it with the sample and compare with the expected result

Do this
  1. 1Download the 4 sample files and upload them to Input
  2. 2In Jonas's panel, click ▶
  3. 3Open the file LABORCLAIM_….md in Output

[Text of petition.pdf, 9 pages. Fictitious initial petition.]
TO THE HONORABLE JUDGE OF THE 99TH LABOR COURT OF SÃO PAULO
JOANA MOREIRA DINIZ, CPF 000.123.456-00, resident in São Paulo/SP, files a LABOR CLAIM against BOM LAR VAREJO S.A.

THE CONTRACT
The claimant worked as a cashier at store 0142, from May 2022 to June 2026, when she was dismissed without cause.

THE WORKING HOURS
She worked from 10 a.m. to 8 p.m., Monday to Saturday, throughout the contract, without payment for the excess hours. She had only 30 minutes of meal break. From January to June 2026, she closed the register until 11:30 p.m., without receiving the night shift premium.

THE HARASSMENT
The store manager demanded targets by shouting in front of customers. As a result, the claimant developed an anxiety condition (ICD F41.1), as per the attached medical certificate. Her coworker Rita de Cássia Prado witnessed the facts and will be heard as a witness.

THE TERMINATION
The severance pay was paid 18 days after the termination.

THE CLAIMS
a) overtime and its effects: R$ 28,600.00;
b) suppressed intra-day break: R$ 9,150.00;
c) night shift premium from January to June 2026: R$ 6,480.00;
d) compensation for moral damages: R$ 25,000.00;
e) fine under art. 477 of the CLT (labor code): R$ 2,380.00.
The claim is valued at R$ 71,610.00.

Documents attached: power of attorney; digital work card (CTPS); 4 pay slips; termination statement; medical certificate; 2 screenshots of app conversations.

Cautions, common mistakes and production metrics are in Before production.

Before production

Cautions

The hearing date and any deadline are transcribed from the law firm's email; the employee never calculates deadlines for the defense, appeals or filings, because the count depends on procedural rules and local holidays, which are the lawyer's responsibility. Each lawsuit is read on its own and nothing from another former employee's complaint at the same store completes claims or facts. Witness names and health data stay in the case folder, out of the spreadsheet shared with HR. A claimant who was not found requires human verification before the request to HR.

Common mistakes

  • Adding up the claims and reporting the total as the amount in controversy when the complaint states a different amount; the divergence is information for the lawyer, not an error to correct.
  • Requesting time cards from HR without the period; 12 months arrive and the defense loses the earlier years.
  • Identifying the claimant by name only; a namesake in a 9-thousand-employee chain leads to the wrong store.
  • Classifying the claim by the title of the complaint's section rather than by what is actually being claimed.

Metrics

MetricRangeSource
Analyst's time per new casefrom 50 minutes to 10 to 15 minutes of checkingestimate based on the described routine
Claims matching the analyst's sheet in calibration90% or more, amount in controversy in 100%estimate based on the described routine
Defenses filed without a document for the period claimedfrom 1 in 5 to less than 1 in 20estimate based on the described routine

Sample production output

Fictional sample. Sheet for case 0001234-56.2026 (fictional), 3rd Labor Court, received from Law Firm B on 2026-09-02.
Claimant: former employee ID 48812, cashier, store 0077 (Curitiba), hired 2023-02-13, dismissed 2026-03-20 by the employer without cause. Found in the base by name and by the period stated in the complaint.
Amount in controversy stated in the complaint: R$ 68,420.00. Hearing: 2026-11-04 at 9:20 a.m., as reported by the law firm in the email; I did not check or calculate any deadline.
Claim 1 | OVERTIME | alleges working hours from 8 a.m. to 7 p.m. with 2 days off a month, whole period | amount assigned R$ 31,200.00 | documents from HR: time cards from 2023-02 to 2026-03, hours compensation agreement, days-off schedule.
Claim 2 | BREAK | alleges a 20-minute break | R$ 12,800.00 | documents: time cards (same), internal break policy.
Claim 3 | MORAL DAMAGES | alleges pressure over targets with exposure in a messaging group | R$ 15,000.00 | documents: targets policy, store manager's training records, contact for the store manager at the time.
Claim 4 | SEVERANCE PAY | difference in the FGTS (severance fund) penalty | R$ 9,420.00 | documents: termination agreement, FGTS statement, proof of payment.
Documents filed by the claimant: 3 pages of app messages, termination agreement, 2 pay slips. Note: the complaint requests testimony from a witness identified as a former colleague at store 0077; name recorded only in the case folder.
